_notes: Verified 2026-09-17 against live provider APIs with the keys present in .env.
openai-small -> gpt-4.1-nano  VERIFIED in GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models (cheapest small non-reasoning)
anthropic-haiku -> claude-haiku-4-5  VERIFIED in GET https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models; the OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions accepts stream:true, so no Messages-API adapter is used

cerebras-oss120 -> gpt-oss-120b  VERIFIED. Reasoning: only 'low'|'medium'|'high' exist ('none'/'minimal' are rejected with wrong_api_format). With no reasoning_effort a 20-token call spends every token on reasoning and returns content:null; reasoning_effort:'low' returns visible content (3 reasoning tokens).

cerebras-qwen38 -> qwen-3.8-27b  VERIFIED. 'chat_template_kwargs' is REJECTED by Cerebras ('property unsupported') — the previous config here was broken. 'disable_reasoning': true works and gives 0 reasoning tokens with visible content.

mercury-2.5 -> mercury-2.5  VERIFIED in GET https://api.inceptionlabs.ai/v1/models (mercury-2 also present). Tunable reasoning: reasoning_effort:'none' is accepted and gives 0 reasoning tokens with visible content; 'low', reasoning:{enabled:false}, thinking:false and diffusing_effort all leave it thinking and return empty content. Prices below are the ones the /models endpoint reports (0.04 / 0.15 per 1M).

openrouter-* -> VERIFIED. Provider pinning {provider:{order:['Groq'],allow_fallbacks:false}} returns provider:'Groq'; {provider:{sort:'throughput'}} also resolved to Groq on 2026-09-17. Per-provider prices read from GET /api/v1/models/<model>/endpoints: Groq gpt-oss-20b 0.075/0.30, Groq gpt-oss-120b 0.15/0.60.
Groq direct (groq-oss20 / groq-oss120) has no key — Shahmir could not get a developer plan. Those two entries stay and hide themselves; the OpenRouter-pinned equivalents are the route to Groq.

All usd_in/usd_out are USD per 1M tokens.
cerebras-qwen38 needs the raised desktop cap: at 7,000 it hit finish_reason=length on 5 of 6 desktops and lost the taskbar/templates to truncation.
SPEC §12.1 / I7 budgets (2026-09-17): boot 800, desktop 3500, app 2500, page 2500, repair 3500. Speed is the product; volume is not.

json_mode: the engine accepts response_format:{type:'json_object'} on /chat/completions. Set only where verified — Cerebras and OpenRouter document it, OpenAI has it, Anthropic's compatibility endpoint does not. Used ONLY by the kind=identity fallback call (I1); no HTML kind ever asks for JSON.

timeout_ms (S4): per-engine wall clock for one generation, overriding GEN_TIMEOUT_MS. anthropic-haiku gets 60000 because BAKEOFF-2 measured its desktops at a median total_ms of 25,003 — exactly our own 25 s cap — and two of four boots died on it.
cerebras-qwen38's 12,000-token override is REMOVED: SPEC §12.8 says qwen is out unless the budget cut tames it, so it now runs on the same 3,500 as everything else and the next bake-off decides.

identity budget raised 300 -> 500 (v0.2): gpt-oss spends reasoning tokens out of max_tokens, so a 300-token identity call came back truncated mid-JSON on cerebras — measured, both with and without response_format. 500 costs $0.00035 and is only ever paid on the I1 rescue path.

H1 routes (2026-09-17, v0.3): engine:'auto' resolves through `routes.default` per kind. Primary cerebras-oss120, hedge or-oss120-groq (the same gpt-oss-120b weights behind Groq, so the prompt needs no per-engine wording and the documents are the same shape). boot/desktop start both at once (HEDGE_AFTER_MS_BOOT=0) because the whole product is the first second; app/page wait HEDGE_AFTER_MS=900 for a content token first. An explicit engine id bypasses routing AND hedging so single engines stay judgeable.

boot budget 800 -> 1600 (2026-09-17, MEASURED by scripts/boot-budget.mjs, 6 calls, $0.011): max_tokens on Cerebras gpt-oss-120b INCLUDES reasoning tokens. At 800 the cap bound at exactly completion_tokens=800 with finish_reason=length on 2 of 3 calls, reasoning_tokens 357-659, one document left at 507 visible characters. At 1600 the model stopped on its own at 739-1005 completion tokens on 3 of 3 (finish_reason=stop), reasoning 301-629, documents 1,206-1,385 characters. So the raise costs nothing on a normal boot -- it is never reached -- and removes the starvation case that made a boot screen paint nothing. SPEC 12.1's brevity now rests on the prompt, which is where it was already argued.

app 2500 -> 4000, page 2500 -> 3200, repair 3500 -> 4000 (2026-09-17, MEASURED by scripts/kind-budget.mjs, 54 calls, $0.137; reviews/BUDGET-2.md): the same arithmetic as the boot raise, run on the document kinds. The probe reproduced HANDOFF-5's blank-ish app window exactly -- kind=app on `photos` hit finish_reason=length 1 of 3 at 2500 and left an UNCLOSED document, while the same app at 4000 stopped on its own at 1927-2278 completion tokens. Every other shape measured was far inside its cap: desktop p100 1864 of 3500, notes 1703, browser 1034, a reference page 1604 and a search-results page 1366. Raising a cap did NOT raise output -- medians were flat or lower at the higher budget, i.e. these documents are prompt-bound, not budget-bound -- so the raise buys headroom and is billed only on tokens actually produced. Its real price is the PRE-RESERVATION against MAX_USD_PER_DAY (server/index.ts estimates a generation at costUsd(engine, promptTokens, maxTokensFor(kind))), which is ~$0.001 more per app generation at $25/day. desktop stays 3500 and boot stays 1600 (53 clean boots); repair follows desktop's old shape and is now app's, because a repair rewrites the whole document that ran out of room.
